headline: Daily research brief — Sunday, October 18

items.detail: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said Saturday that two oil tankers (each carrying ~2M barrels) caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz — an unconfirmed tactical escalation from projectile attacks to area-denial. Iran's foreign minister said Sunday that Iran's offer to reopen the strait within seven days is still on the table, but the preconditions are incompatible as stated (lifting the blockade vs addressing the nuclear program first), so the offer is a floor under resolution, not a priceable event. CENTCOM reports ~400 vessels and ~100M barrels moved safely under escort in the week ending Oct 17. Friday's closes: Brent $109.86 (+3.7%, highest since May), WTI $101.41 (+3.5%). The first market price read comes at ~15:00 PT Sunday when futures reopen.
items.title: Hormuz escalation meets a diplomatic floor — Sunday 15:00 PT futures reopen is the first price read

items.detail: The FRED pull (as of Oct 18) carries no new observations — bond markets closed Sunday, so every series still ends Oct 15, an identical observation set to yesterday. Effective fed funds 3.88%, 2Y 4.77%, 10Y 5.10%. The 2s10s spread is +33 bp, unchanged day-over-day; the curve has flattened 52→33 bp over 60 days with the front end pinned. The 10Y is 21 bp off its Oct 5 peak of 5.31% — mild relief, not a regime change, and 5.10% remains a standing discount-rate headwind on growth multiples (duration-heavy NVDA and TSLA most exposed). SOFR exceeds fed funds by 1 bp: funding orderly, no stress signal. The next data point is Monday's pull covering Friday Oct 16.
